verdict.why: The video hooks the viewer instantly by opening on a finished 3D result rather than a loading screen or terminal. The large, explicit captions make the problem, the validation method, and the final pass rate entirely understandable without sound.
fixes: Enlarge the individual labels in the 3D model grids so they remain legible on smaller screens.
Stagger the appearance of the dense statistical text on the final summary slides so the viewer has time to process each point.

verdict.why: The finished renders appear immediately and look polished, but narrow source views, small captions, and dense grids weaken phone legibility. The captions establish a 30-of-32 rendering result and explain the checks, though the long showcase makes the engineering achievement less striking than the artwork.
fixes: Enlarge the opening claim and captions for phone viewing, keeping the finished render visible.
Cut the loading sequence and repeated showcase shots into a shorter selection of three contrasting results.
Show the command, resulting screenshots, and 30/32 verdict together early so the automation is unmistakable.
Replace the dense result grids with larger paged examples and clearly labeled failures.
Explain the checks in plain language and clarify why setup mentions 8 sandboxes while validation mentions 17.
